newsitem.title: GERMANY: Analysts' comment on Lufthansa revamp.
newsitem.headline: Analysts' comment on Lufthansa revamp.

text.p: Following is a selection of aviation analysts' comments on the announcement by German national carrier Deutsche Lufthansa AG that it plans to shed at least 10 percent of management staff in a revamp to prepare for increased competition after full liberalisation of the European aviation market this year.
The airline said it would group all its passenger services in a separate division which will act as a profit centre and it will have its own divisional management board.

UWE WEINREICH, AVIATION ANALYST, BHF-BANK : "It makes sense if responsibility for costs and earnings is placed with a new layer of management and it makes sense to combine activities which belong together under one management. We have had a buy recommendation for the past 14 days and we see earnings-per-share of 1.15 marks for 1996, rising to 1.62 marks in 1997 and 1.95 marks in 1998. I don't think Lufthansa will be dramatically affected by the liberalisation of the European air market this year, the German domestic routes are not very profitable and there is a limit to to the number of airlines willing to compete on them."

HEINZ WEYERSHAEUSER, DEUTSCHE GENOSSENSCHAFTSBANK: "It doesn't necessarily mean they will become more efficient in their operating business. Daimler-Benz AG has done virtually the opposite (by integrating its car subsidiary Mercedes-Benz AG into the Daimler group and making the Daimler group management board responsible for Mercedes) and Daimler's move was welcomed by investors. I would see Lufthansa's change as neutral and do not see it as a reason to change my "hold" recommendation for the shares. In the short-term I see the share price coming under pressure because a strike by the DAG union cannot be ruled out and because 1996 earnings will certainly show a fall from 1995. Com

One analyst at a German bank who declined to be named said the changes amounted only a small "mosaic piece" within the airline's wider restructuring. "The cost savings resulting from this are small compared with Lufthansa's overall cost savings aims."
